result.title: A Search Worth a Billion Pixels: Explaining Gigapixel Classifiers
result.summary: Perturbation-based attribution methods explain model predictions without accessing their internal representations, but scaling them to high-resolution images requires balancing perturbation granularity and computational cost. Fine-grained perturbations require many model evaluations, whereas coarse masks may overlook small but relevant evidence. We introduce Wavelet Find-and-Refine (WaFR), a model-agnostic attribution method combining adaptive hierarchical search with sparse multiscale regression. By selectively refining regions that influence the prediction, WaFR maintains fine-grained localisation with a computational cost that depends on the spatial distribution of the evidence. As image resolution increases to 8,192 pixels per side, WaFR maintains a Pointing Game score of at least .995 in controlled localisation experiments, including at matched forward-pass budgets. On gigapixel whole-slide images, it requires a median of 176 forward passes and achieves the highest mean patch-level AUROC among the evaluated perturbation-based methods (.949).

AI.brief_summary: 提出无模型归因方法 WaFR，用自适应层次搜索加稀疏多尺度回归，只在影响预测的区域细化扰动，在千兆像素全切片图像上以百余次前向获得高定位精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先粗定位、再按证据空间分布分配细化预算」的层次搜索思路，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、证据区域定位与 look/stop 计算分配提供可供核查的线索，但原文不涉及多模态推理或 latent 状态。
